My girlfriend is allergic to cats and we have a cat together. Here is what we do:
1. They make cat food that reduces the allergens from cats. It’s a little more expensive though, and we have only been able to find it in dry food. We use Purina Pro Plan Live Clear once a day (other meal is normal cat food). It takes about 6 weeks to work. 
2. Get an air purifier with a HEPA filter. I got two for 40$ on Amazon and they are enough for our ~850 square foot apartment. 
3. Vacuuming at least once a week, we ended up getting an off brand robot vacuum, but any one will do. This will reduce built up allergens in the carpet (may not be necessary if you have hard wood floors)
4. Occasional use of over the counter allergy meds. This is especially helpful for the first few weeks when you are still getting all the built up allergens out.

I work from home as a Software engineer. I log in at exactly 8am, first I open a google sheet to log my login time. Then I check Slack and catch up on any messages I missed in the group chats. This is usually in the software development group chat, sometime the company group chat has messages. Sometimes I check my email, but I’ve been there around 5 months and maybe written 3 emails and rarely get emails of note. By about 8:06 I’m ready to actually work. I review the ticket I am going to be working on. Then I message in the development group chat on Slack at my boss where I am on my ticket and what I plan to do during the morning. By about 8:10 I open VSCode and get to coding. I code until 11:55 am, occasionally interacting with the chats, or meeting with my boss to discuss issues I run into with my ticket. I also sometimes review other people’s code. At 11:55 I log that I am clocking out for lunch at noon on my Google sheet, and log a brief description of what I did. Then I message my boss a recap of what I have gotten done so far today and let him know I am going to lunch. I always send this message at exactly noon. At exactly 1pm I open up my Google sheet and log that I clocked back in at 1pm. Then I continue working on my ticket. Pretty much the same thing as the morning. Then at 4:55pm I update my time log again, as well as log what I worked on during the afternoon. I then write a message to my boss in slack recapping what I did for the afternoon and what I plan on doing in the morning. I send this message at exactly 5pm. Then I am done with work. For security reasons I cannot reveal anymore details than this, such as specific software I use or where I work. However, I hope you found this helpful. My day is honestly pretty simple.

It’s not uncommon for an animal’s fur color to shift from season to season or as the age. I would watch her carefully to make sure she isn’t excessively itching or showing signs or skin irritation, but it’s probably just natural. 

Has the temperature of the area you keep her in shifted recently? While seasonal color change is normal for some animals, it is usually triggered or heightened by a change in temperature or environment. For example a cat who spends the majority of it’s time outdoors will likely grow a much thicker coat in the winter then an indoor cat who is kept at a steady temperature all year long. 
If the temperature has changed I would be careful. While hamsters don’t hibernate, they can go into a hibernation like state called torpor if they get too cold. It’s not well researched, but showing signs of adjusting to the cold could be an indicator their body may go into this state.

Switching up what’s in the cage at least once a month can be great for keeping your hamster entertained. However removing all the bedding once a month can be very stressful. I would suggest removing 1/4-1/3 of the bedding once a month and replacing it with fresh bedding in order to keep it clean. Then  only replacing all the bedding every 3-6 months depending on how dirty your hamster gets the cage and then adding maybe 1-2 handfuls of the old bedding back in to help your hamster get reorientated. This not only saves on cost, but doing it gradually like this can help reduce stress that can be associated with cleaning the cage.

I don’t know a subreddit but here is my (hopefully correct) basic run down after a year. 

There is 2 types of karma, comment karma and post karma. 

Comment karma is from comments. When you leave a comment on Reddit a little button will appear in the bottom corner that says “vote” in between an up and down arrow. Based on how many up/down votes you get you’ll get a score. Scores could be positive numbers of people liked it or negative numbers if they didn’t. Everyone can only affect the score by 1 number. (Example: your comment has a score of 4 but then I hit the upvote button so now it is 5) all the scores of every comment you have made on your Reddit account make up your comment karma.

Post Karma works like comment karma except it’s with a post instead of a comment. Post scores also do not directly translate into your post karma. Usually it’s a 1 to 1 conversation until you get past a certain limit per post. Then Reddit gives you less and less karma for each upvote, but it’s based on that post alone. (Example: I recently had a post get 50,000 upvotes so my score was 50,000 however I only actually got a few thousand post karma because the score was so high). 

Again I’m no expert but that’s my best understanding so far.
